title: Restaurant sales and temperature
data: Larry's Commissary, 312 trading days in 2018 (salesData + weatherData + gameData)

questions.prompt: Predict daily sales for an observation with max temperature = 60 that is in the group "game day".
questions.equation: Predicted daily sales = b₀ + b₁[Max temperature] + b₂[Game day]

checks.label: Predicted daily sales

answer: Substitute Max temperature = 60 and Game day = 1 into the model:
Max temperature = 60 is inside the observed range (28.94 to 104), so this is interpolation, not extrapolation.

questions.prompt: Interpret the coefficient on max temperature. By how much does predicted daily sales change when max temperature increases by 10?
questions.equation: Predicted daily sales = a₀ + a₁[Max temperature]

checks.label: Change for +10 max temperature
Significant at the 5% level?

answer: a₁ = 7.580: each one-unit increase in max temperature (tmax (°F)) is associated with an increase of 7.580 in predicted daily sales (total netTotal for the day (USD)).
p = 0.008 < 0.05: statistically significant at the 5% level.
Association, not causation: this is observational data, other factors are not held constant in a one-variable model.

questions.prompt: What do you learn from the p-value of the max temperature-squared term?
questions.equation: Predicted daily sales = c₀ + c₁[Max temperature] + c₂[Max temperature]²

checks.label: Is the squared term significant at 5%?
Shape implied by the sign of c₂

answer: p < 0.05: there is statistically significant curvature – the effect of max temperature on daily sales is not constant but weakens as max temperature increases.
A negative c₂ means a inverted-U (concave) curve.

questions.prompt: Interpret all coefficients in context: the intercept, max temperature, game day, and max temperature × game day.
questions.equation: Predicted daily sales = d₀ + d₁[Max temperature] + d₂[Game day] + d₃([Max temperature]×[Game day])

checks.label: Slope of max temperature for the group "game day"
Predicted difference (game day minus no game) at max temperature = 60
Is the interaction significant at 5%?

answer: d₀ = 2,710.0: predicted daily sales for the reference group (no game) when max temperature = 0 – zero may lie outside the data, so it is mainly an anchor.
d₁ = 6.943: slope of max temperature for the reference group.
d₂ = 437.5: difference between game day and the reference group when max temperature = 0.
d₃ = 13.810 (p = 0.414): how much the slope differs for game day. Their slope is d₁ + d₃ = 20.7530. Not significant at 5% – no evidence that the slopes differ.
At max temperature = 60 the predicted gap is d₂ + d₃×60 = 1,266.1000.
